title: Route by the need, not the level
statement: Route learners who need more comprehension help by their specific need, vocabulary and background knowledge, strategy or text structure, not by a global reading level.
detail: An IES video on when to use small groups in teaching reading comprehension, quoted in a reading course's review standard, notes that a recent meta-analysis found no research to support level-based grouping and advises grouping by students' specific assessed needs: some need more work on vocabulary and background knowledge, others more strategy instruction or attention to text structure (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/teaching-moves/branch-by-need-profile.md`). The standard's design infers that need from the learner's errors, so two learners who missed the same item can go down different tracks, and it never answers a miss by pushing an easier passage on the same skill. The video does not name the meta-analysis.
against: The same standard's curriculum criteria say the course does not rely on a diagnostic test to find knowledge or comprehension gaps, since a valid one does not exist, and build breadth of knowledge instead (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/dimensions/D7-knowledge-first-curriculum.md`, line 35).

evidence.quote: It's important to note that in a recent meta-analysis, there was no research found to support level-based grouping.
Rather, when you're grouping students for reading comprehension or for anything, you want to look at their specific assess needs.
some students are likely to need more work on vocabulary and background knowledge building, whereas other students might benefit from more strategy instruction or more attention to text structure.
When a child fails a comprehension item, the router does not push an easier passage on the same skill
two children who both missed the same item can be sent down *different* tracks

citations.ref: When should teachers use small groups in teaching reading comprehension?, REL West video
